lines.text: Paul starts with where the believers in Ephesus used to be: dead in their trespasses and sins, walking in them, going along with the ways of this world and the ruler of the power of the air. Not napping, friend. DEAD.
And Paul says all of us lived that way once, fulfilling the cravings of the flesh. By nature we were children of the devil. But God, rich in mercy, steps in because of His great love for us.

God made us alive with Christ even when we were dead in our trespasses. "It is by grace you have been saved!" Then He raised us up with Christ and seated us with Him in the heavenly realms. Front-row seat, baker, and I never even bought a ticket.

Why? So that in the coming ages He can display the surpassing riches of His grace. We're saved by grace through faith. It's the gift of God, not by works, so no one can boast. Nobody's bragging about their batch on this one.
We are God's temple, created in Christ Jesus to do good works that God prepared in advance as our way of life. And God doesn't stamp crooked.
